paras.en: The sixth planet was a planet ten times as large. An old gentleman lived there and wrote enormous books.
paras.zh: 第六颗星球是一颗有十倍那么大的星球。上面住着一位老先生，写着一本本硕大的书。

paras.en: “Oh! Here’s an explorer!” he cried when he caught sight of the little prince.
paras.zh: “咦！来了一位探险家！”他一看见小王子，就叫了起来。

paras.en: The little prince sat down on the table and caught his breath for a moment. He had already travelled so much!
paras.zh: 小王子坐到桌子上，歇了口气。他已经走过那么多地方了！

paras.en: “Where do you come from?” the old gentleman asked him.
paras.zh: “你从哪里来？”老先生问他。

paras.en: “What is that big book?” said the little prince. “What do you do here?”
paras.zh: “这本大书是什么书？”小王子说，“您在这里做什么？”

paras.en: “I am a geographer,” said the old gentleman.
paras.zh: “我是地理学家。”老先生说。

paras.en: “What is a geographer?”
paras.zh: “什么是地理学家？”

paras.en: “A scholar who knows where the seas, rivers, towns, mountains and deserts are.”
paras.zh: “就是知道海、河流、城市、山脉和沙漠都在哪里的学者。”

paras.en: “Now that is very interesting,” said the little prince. “Now that is a real job at last!” And he glanced around him at the geographer’s planet. He had never seen such a majestic planet before.
paras.zh: “这可真有意思，”小王子说，“这总算是一份真正的工作了！”他朝四周望了一眼，看看地理学家的星球。他还从没见过这样雄伟的星球。

paras.en: “Your planet is very beautiful. Are there any oceans?”
paras.zh: “您的星球真美。这里有大洋吗？”

paras.en: “I have no way of knowing,” said the geographer.
paras.zh: “我没法知道。”地理学家说。

paras.en: “Oh!” (The little prince was disappointed.) “And mountains?”
paras.zh: “啊！”（小王子很失望。）“那山呢？”

paras.en: “I have no way of knowing,” said the geographer.
paras.zh: “我没法知道。”地理学家说。

paras.en: “And cities and rivers and deserts?”
paras.zh: “那城市呢，河流呢，沙漠呢？”

paras.en: “I have no way of knowing that either,” said the geographer.
paras.zh: “这些我也没法知道。”地理学家说。

paras.en: “But you are a geographer!”
paras.zh: “可您是地理学家呀！”

paras.en: “That is true,” said the geographer, “but I am not an explorer. I have no explorers at all. It is not the geographer who goes out to count the cities, rivers, mountains, seas, oceans and deserts. The geographer is too important to wander about. He does not leave his office. But he receives explorers there. He questions them and writes down what they remember. And if what one of them remembers seems interesting to him, the geographer makes enquiries into the explorer’s moral character.”
paras.zh: “没错，”地理学家说，“但我不是探险家。我这里一个探险家也没有。出去清点城市、河流、山、海、洋和沙漠的，不是地理学家。地理学家太重要了，不能到处闲逛。他不离开自己的办公室。不过，他在那里接待探险家。他向他们提问，把他们记得的事情记录下来。如果其中一个人记得的事情让他觉得有趣，地理学家就会调查这位探险家的品行。”

paras.en: “Why is that?”
paras.zh: “为什么呢？”

paras.en: “Because an explorer who told lies would cause disasters in geography books. And so would an explorer who drank too much.”
paras.zh: “因为探险家要是说谎，就会给地理书带来灾难。探险家要是喝太多酒，也会这样。”

paras.en: “Why is that?” asked the little prince.
paras.zh: “为什么呢？”小王子问。

paras.en: “Because drunkards see double. So the geographer would write down two mountains where there is only one.”
paras.zh: “因为酒鬼看东西有重影。这样一来，明明只有一座山，地理学家却会记成两座。”

paras.en: “I know someone,” said the little prince, “who would make a bad explorer.”
paras.zh: “我认识一个人，”小王子说，“他要是当探险家，一定当不好。”

paras.en: “That is possible. So, when the explorer seems to be of good character, we have his discovery investigated.”
paras.zh: “有这个可能。所以，当探险家的品行看起来不错时，我们就请人调查他的发现。”

paras.en: “Do you go and look?”
paras.zh: “去看看吗？”

paras.en: “No. It is too complicated. But we require the explorer to provide proof. If, for example, he has discovered a big mountain, we require him to bring back big stones from it.”
paras.zh: “不。那太麻烦了。不过，我们要求探险家拿出证据。比如说，要是他发现了一座大山，我们就要求他从那里带回大石头。”

paras.en: The geographer suddenly grew excited.
paras.zh: 地理学家忽然激动起来。

paras.en: “But you—you have come from far away! You are an explorer! You are going to describe your planet to me!”
paras.zh: “可是你，你是从远方来的！你就是探险家！你要给我讲讲你的星球！”

paras.en: And the geographer opened his register and sharpened his pencil. Explorers’ accounts are first written down in pencil. To write them down in ink, we wait until the explorer has provided proof.
paras.zh: 于是，地理学家打开登记簿，削起铅笔来。探险家的讲述，先用铅笔记下。要等探险家拿出证据，才用墨水记下来。

paras.en: “Well?” asked the geographer.
paras.zh: “那么？”地理学家问。

paras.en: “Oh! Where I live,” said the little prince, “it is not very interesting. It is tiny. I have three volcanoes. Two active volcanoes, and one extinct volcano. But you never know.”
paras.zh: “哦！我住的地方，”小王子说，“没什么趣味，小得很。我有三座火山。两座活火山，还有一座死火山。不过，谁也说不准。”

paras.en: “You never know,” said the geographer.
paras.zh: “这可说不准。”地理学家说。

paras.en: “I also have a flower.”
paras.zh: “我还有一朵花。”

paras.en: “We do not record flowers,” said the geographer.
paras.zh: “我们不记录花。”地理学家说。

paras.en: “Why not! They’re the prettiest things!”
paras.zh: “为什么呀！花是最好看的！”

paras.en: “Because flowers are ephemeral.”
paras.zh: “因为花是短暂的。”

paras.en: “What does ‘ephemeral’ mean?”
paras.zh: “‘短暂’是什么意思？”

paras.en: “Geography books,” said the geographer, “are the most serious of all books. They never go out of date. It is very rare for a mountain to change places. It is very rare for an ocean to lose all its water. We write about things that last for ever.”
paras.zh: “地理书，”地理学家说，“是所有书里最严肃的书。它们永远不会过时。一座山换个地方，是很少见的。一片海洋的水全部流空，是很少见的。我们写的是永恒的事物。”

paras.en: “But extinct volcanoes can wake up,” the little prince interrupted. “What does ‘ephemeral’ mean?”
paras.zh: “可是熄灭的火山也会醒来呀，”小王子打断了他，“‘短暂’是什么意思？”

paras.en: “Whether volcanoes are extinct or awake, it is all the same to us,” said the geographer. “What matters to us is the mountain. It does not change.”
paras.zh: “火山是熄灭了还是醒着，对我们来说都一样，”地理学家说，“我们看重的是山。山是不会变的。”

paras.en: “But what does ‘ephemeral’ mean?” repeated the little prince, who had never in his life given up on a question once he had asked it.
paras.zh: “可是，‘短暂’是什么意思？”小王子又问了一遍。他这辈子只要提出了一个问题，就从来不会放下不问。

paras.en: “It means ‘in danger of disappearing soon’.”
paras.zh: “意思就是‘有很快消失的危险’。”

paras.en: “My flower is in danger of disappearing soon?”
paras.zh: “我的花有很快消失的危险？”

paras.en: “Of course.”
paras.zh: “当然。”

paras.en: My flower is short-lived, the little prince said to himself, and she has only four thorns to defend herself against the world! And I have left her all alone at home!
paras.zh: 我的花生命短暂，小王子心想，她只有四根刺，来保护自己，对抗整个世界！可我却把她独自留在了家里！

paras.en: That was his first stirring of regret. But he found his courage again:
paras.zh: 这是他头一次感到后悔。但他又鼓起勇气：

paras.en: “Where would you advise me to go and visit?” he asked.
paras.zh: “您建议我去哪里看看呢？”他问。

paras.en: “The planet Earth,” the geographer replied. “It has a good reputation...”
paras.zh: “地球这颗行星，”地理学家回答他，“它的名声很好……”

paras.en: And the little prince went away, thinking of his flower.
paras.zh: 于是小王子走了，心里想着他的花。
